question.stem: The product formed from the following reaction sequence is

steps: Step 1: LiAlH4 reduces the nitrile group (-C≡N) fully to a primary amine: PhCN → PhCH2NH2 (benzylamine).
Step 2: NaNO2 + HCl generates nitrous acid (HNO2) in situ, which diazotises the primary aliphatic amine to form an unstable alkyl diazonium salt, PhCH2N2+Cl-.
Step 3: Aliphatic diazonium salts are unstable even at low temperature and decompose immediately via an SN1-type mechanism, releasing N2 gas and forming a carbocation (PhCH2+).
Step 4: Water (H2O) attacks the benzylic carbocation to give the final product, benzyl alcohol (PhCH2OH), matching option 2.
ai_solution.html:
1. Step 1: LiAlH4 reduces the nitrile group (-C≡N) fully to a primary amine: PhCN → PhCH2NH2 (benzylamine).
  2. Step 2: NaNO2 + HCl generates nitrous acid (HNO2) in situ, which diazotises the primary aliphatic amine to form an unstable alkyl diazonium salt, PhCH2N2+Cl-.
  3. Step 3: Aliphatic diazonium salts are unstable even at low temperature and decompose immediately via an SN1-type mechanism, releasing N2 gas and forming a carbocation (PhCH2+).
  4. Step 4: Water (H2O) attacks the benzylic carbocation to give the final product, benzyl alcohol (PhCH2OH), matching option 2.
ai_solution.why: LiAlH4 reduces PhCN to PhCH2NH2 (benzylamine); diazotisation of this primary aliphatic amine with NaNO2/HCl forms an unstable diazonium salt that loses N2 in water to give benzyl alcohol (PhCH2OH).

chapter.name: Amines
chapter.why: The answer depends on reducing benzonitrile to benzylamine with LiAlH4 and then on the reaction of a primary aliphatic amine with nitrous acid (NaNO2 + HCl) followed by H2O, which gives benzyl alcohol. Both steps are taught in the Amines chapter.

subtopics.name: Chemical Reactions of Amines (Carbylamine, Nitrous Acid, Arylsulphonyl Chloride and Electrophilic Substitution Reactions)
subtopics.why: The answer (benzyl alcohol) depends on benzonitrile being reduced by LiAlH4 to benzylamine, a primary aliphatic amine that reacts with nitrous acid (NaNO2 + HCl) to give an unstable diazonium salt which hydrolyses to the alcohol.

subtopics.name: Methods of Preparation of Amines
subtopics.why: Step (i) of the sequence, LiAlH4 reduction of benzonitrile to benzylamine, is a method of preparing amines, and getting that intermediate right is what makes the later nitrous acid step give a benzylic alcohol.

step_list: Recognise LiAlH4 reduces the nitrile C≡N all the way to a primary amine, giving benzylamine (not an aldehyde, not an amide)
Treat benzylamine with NaNO2/HCl: a PRIMARY ALIPHATIC amine gives a diazonium salt that is unstable at any temperature and loses N2 to give a benzyl cation
Trap the cation with water in step (iii) to give benzyl alcohol, rather than with chloride
difficulty.why: Three linked transformations with three genuinely competing products — the aromatic-vs-aliphatic diazonium distinction and the choice of nucleophile (H2O in step iii vs Cl- from the HCl) both have to be settled, so elimination gives almost nothing and the candidate must reason the whole sequence through.
difficulty.what_makes_it_hard: Organic difficulty of the reaction-condition type: the stem's step (iii) H2O is the only clue separating benzyl alcohol from benzyl chloride, and the most attractive wrong answer (stable diazonium chloride) comes from applying the well-drilled aryl-diazonium rule to an alkyl amine.

Choose the **correct answer** from the options given below :

statements.label: (a)
statements.text: The leaflets are modified into pointed hard thorns in $Citrus$ and $Bougainvillea$

statements.label: (b)
statements.text: Axillary buds form slender and spirally coiled tendrils in cucumber and pumpkin

statements.label: (c)
statements.text: Stem is flattened and fleshy in $Opuntia$ and modified to perform the function of leaves

statements.label: (d)
statements.text: $Rhizophora$ shows vertically upward growing roots that help to get oxygen for respiration

statements.label: (e)
statements.text: Subaerially growing stems in grasses and strawberry help in vegetative propagation

solution.full_text: 1. Axillary buds of stems get modified into woody, straight and pointed thorns. Thorns are found in many plants such as $Citrus$ and $Bougainvillea$.
solution.html: 1. Axillary buds of stems get modified into woody, straight and pointed thorns. Thorns are found in many plants such as Citrus and Bougainvillea.
steps: Axillary buds of stems get modified into woody, straight and pointed thorns. Thorns are found in many plants such as $Citrus$ and $Bougainvillea$.
printed_lines: Axillary buds of stems get modified into woody, straight and pointed thorns. Thorns are found in many
plants such as Citrus and Bougainvillea.

steps: (a) is false: in $Citrus$ and $Bougainvillea$ the thorns are modified axillary buds (stem modification), not leaflets.
(b) is true: stem tendrils arising from axillary buds are slender and spirally coiled in cucumber and pumpkin.
(c) is true: $Opuntia$ has a flattened, fleshy green stem (phylloclade) that performs the function of leaves.
(d) is true: $Rhizophora$ has pneumatophores, roots growing vertically upward to obtain oxygen for respiration.
(e) is true: subaerially growing stems (runners/stolons) in grasses and strawberry help in vegetative propagation.
Correct set is (b), (c), (d) and (e) only, which is option $1$.
ai_solution.html:
1. (a) is false: in Citrus and Bougainvillea the thorns are modified axillary buds (stem modification), not leaflets.
  2. (b) is true: stem tendrils arising from axillary buds are slender and spirally coiled in cucumber and pumpkin.
  3. (c) is true: Opuntia has a flattened, fleshy green stem (phylloclade) that performs the function of leaves.
  4. (d) is true: Rhizophora has pneumatophores, roots growing vertically upward to obtain oxygen for respiration.
  5. (e) is true: subaerially growing stems (runners/stolons) in grasses and strawberry help in vegetative propagation.
  6. Correct set is (b), (c), (d) and (e) only, which is option 1.
ai_solution.why: Thorns of Citrus and Bougainvillea are modified axillary buds (stem), not leaflets, so (a) is false; (b), (c), (d) and (e) are true.

chapter.name: Morphology of Flowering Plants
chapter.why: The answer depends on modifications of stem and root (stem thorns, stem tendrils, phylloclade in Opuntia, pneumatophores in Rhizophora, runners/stolons), which is morphology of flowering plants.

subtopics.name: The Stem
subtopics.why: The answer depends on stem modifications (axillary-bud tendrils, Opuntia phylloclade, subaerial runners/stolons, and that thorns in Citrus/Bougainvillea are stem-derived, not leaflets) combined with the root modification of pneumatophores in Rhizophora.

subtopics.name: The Root
subtopics.why: Statement (d), the upward-growing respiratory roots of Rhizophora, is a root modification and must be judged correct to separate option 3 from option 1.

step_list: Check (a): NCERT says axillary buds become woody pointed thorns in Citrus and Bougainvillea, not leaflets — altered line, false
Check (b): cucumber/pumpkin tendrils are slender spirally coiled axillary buds — true
Check (c): Opuntia phylloclade, flattened fleshy green stem performing the leaf's function — true
Check (d): Rhizophora pneumatophores, vertically upward roots for oxygen — true
Check (e): runners/stolons in grasses and strawberry, subaerial stems aiding vegetative propagation — true
Match the true set (b), (c), (d) and (e) to an option
difficulty.why: Five separate NCERT lines must each be verified before any option can be picked — long to execute even though each check is pure recall — and the two surviving options differ on exactly the one statement that has been subtly rewritten, so elimination does not finish the job.
difficulty.what_makes_it_hard: Statement (a) is the printed NCERT line with one word changed — 'leaflets are modified into thorns' in place of 'axillary buds become thorns' — and a candidate who recognises the Citrus/Bougainvillea example without reading the subject of the sentence lands straight on option 2.

source.note: Words 'correct' and 'correct answer' are printed in bold in the source; marked with ** in stem_en. Genus names (Citrus, Bougainvillea, Opuntia, Rhizophora) are printed in italics.

question.full_text:
Which one of the following plants does **not** show plasticity?
(1) Buttercup
(2) Maize
(3) Cotton
(4) Coriander

  2. (2)Maize
  3. (3)Cotton
  4. (4)Coriander
question.stem: Which one of the following plants does **not** show plasticity?

solution.full_text:
1. Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity e.g. heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur. In such plants, leaves of juvenile plant are different in a shape from those in mature plants.
2. Maize does not show plasticity.

solution.full_text:
1. Chemiosmosis requires a membrane, a proton pump, a proton gradient and ATP synthase. Energy is used to pump protons across a membrane to create a gradient or a high concentration of protons within the thylakoid lumen.
2. The NADP reductase enzyme is located on the stroma side of the membrane. Along with the electrons that come from the acceptor of electrons of PS I, protons are necessary for reduction of $\mathrm{NADP^{+}}$ to $\mathrm{NADPH + H^{+}}$.
3. The process does not involve breaking of electron gradient.

  3. The process does not involve breaking of electron gradient.

In an $\textit{E. Coli}$ strain $i$ gene gets mutated and its product can not bind the inducer molecule. If growth medium is provided with lactose, what will be the outcome?
(1) $z$, $y$, $a$ genes will not be translated
(2) RNA polymerase will bind the promoter region
(3) Only $z$ gene will get transcribed
(4) $z$, $y$, $a$ genes will be transcribed
question.html:
In an E. Coli strain i gene gets mutated and its product can not bind the inducer molecule. If growth medium is provided with lactose, what will be the outcome?
  1. (1)z, y, a genes will not be translated
  2. (2)RNA polymerase will bind the promoter region
  3. (3)Only z gene will get transcribed
  4. (4)z, y, a genes will be transcribed
question.stem: In an $\textit{E. Coli}$ strain $i$ gene gets mutated and its product can not bind the inducer molecule. If growth medium is provided with lactose, what will be the outcome?

options.text: RNA polymerase will bind the promoter region

solution.full_text:
1. As the product of '$i$' gene binds with the operator region and blocks the transcription and translation of $z$, $y$ and $a$ genes.
2. It's product is prevented from binding to the operator by attaching it with the inducer. As the inducer can now no more capable of binding with the repressor, thus, in all the cases, operator always gets attached with the repressor thereby preventing the transcription and transmission of $z$, $y$ and $a$.
3. Even in the presence of lactose, transcription and translation of $z$, $y$ and $a$ would not occur.

step_list: Recall that the i gene codes for the lac repressor protein, not an enzyme of lactose metabolism
Translate the mutation: the repressor retains operator-binding ability but has lost inducer (allolactose/lactose) binding — a super-repressor (i^s) type
Infer that adding lactose can no longer de-repress, so the repressor stays bound at the operator and blocks transcription
Convert 'no transcription' into the option wording — z, y, a mRNA is never made, hence never translated — and reject the option that says polymerase still works
difficulty.why: Hard: four linked inference steps (i gene is the repressor, the mutation is a super-repressor, lactose cannot relieve repression, so the structural genes stay silent) and three of the four options are genuinely in play — the opposite answer (4) is the default careless response and option 2 trades on the promoter/operator confusion, so elimination gives no help.
difficulty.what_makes_it_hard: The stem never names the mutant as a super-repressor; the candidate must build that phenotype from 'cannot bind the inducer', and the presence of lactose is a deliberate trap pointing at the induced-operon answer.

question.full_text:
Which of the following statements **is not** true?
(1) Homology indicates common ancestry
(2) Flippers of penguins and dolphins are a pair of homologous organs
(3) Analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution
(4) Sweet potato and potato is an example of analogy

answer.publisher_text: Flippers of penguins and dolphins are a pair of homologous organs
answer.ai_text: Flippers of penguins and dolphins are a pair of homologous organs

solution.full_text:
1. Option (2) is the correct answer because flippers of penguins and dolphins are analogous organs as they help in swimming but do not have the same structure.
2. Option (1), (3) and (4) are true statements and hence cannot be the correct answer.
3. Homologous organs have the same structure but have different functions according to the needs of the organisms. Hence, homology indicates common ancestry.
4. Analogous structures have developed for the same function but do not show a similarity in structure. Hence, they are a result of convergent evolution.
5. Sweet potato is a root modification for food storage whereas potato is an underground stem modification for storage. Hence they are analogous.

printed_lines: Therefore, after 60 minutes, 60 E.coli cells will have DNA totally free from ^{15}N.

steps: E. coli divides once every $20\,\text{min}$, so in $60\,\text{min}$ there are $\frac{60}{20} = 3$ generations.
Total cells after 3 generations: $10 \times 2^3 = 80$.
Replication is semiconservative: the two original $^{15}N$ strands of each parent DNA stay intact and end up in 2 cells, so cells carrying $^{15}N$ $= 10 \times 2 = 20$.
Cells totally free of $^{15}N$ $= 80 - 20 = 60$, which is option $1$.
ai_solution.html:
1. E. coli divides once every 20 min, so in 60 min there are 6020 = 3 generations.
  2. Total cells after 3 generations: 10 × 23 = 80.
  3. Replication is semiconservative: the two original 15N strands of each parent DNA stay intact and end up in 2 cells, so cells carrying 15N = 10 × 2 = 20.
  4. Cells totally free of 15N = 80 - 20 = 60, which is option 1.
ai_solution.why: E. coli divides every 20 min, so 3 generations in 60 min give 80 cells; semiconservative replication leaves 20 hybrid cells, so 60 cells are free of 15N.

step_list: Recall the unstated assumption that E. coli generation time is 20 minutes, so 60 min = 3 divisions
Compute final cell number: 10 x 2^3 = 80 cells (each with one dsDNA molecule)
Apply semi-conservative replication: the 20 original 15N strands are conserved and distributed into 20 separate DNA molecules
Subtract: 80 - 20 = 60 cells whose DNA is totally free of 15N

difficulty.what_makes_it_hard: The 20-minute generation time is never stated and must be supplied from memory; and the question asks for cells 'totally free' of 15N, the single keyword that flips the answer from 20 to 60 or from 80 to 60.

solution.full_text:
1. Option (4) is the correct answer as genetically engineered insulin has A-peptide and B-peptide chains of insulin which are produced separately in $E.coli$, then they are extracted and combined by creating disulphide bond between them.
2. Statement (a) is incorrect as genetically engineered insulin does not have an extra stretch of C-peptide.
3. Statement (c) is incorrect as insulin obtained from cattles and pigs is not genetically engineered insulin.
4. Statement (d) is incorrect because conversion of pro-insulin to insulin is not required during production of insulin by genetic engineering as A-peptide and B-peptide chains are produced separately.
5. Statement (e) is incorrect as allergic reactions to insulin are mostly seen when the insulin is obtained from animals.

question.full_text:
If a colour blind female marries a man whose mother was also colour blind, what are the chances of her progeny having colour blindness?
(1) $75\%$
(2) $100\%$
(3) $25\%$
(4) $50\%$

  1. (1)75%
  2. (2)100%
  3. (3)25%
  4. (4)50%
question.stem: If a colour blind female marries a man whose mother was also colour blind, what are the chances of her progeny having colour blindness?

solution.full_text: 1. If mother of man is colourblind, then man will also be colourblind as colour blindness is a X-linked recessive trait and shows criss-cross inheritance.
solution.html: 1. If mother of man is colourblind, then man will also be colourblind as colour blindness is a X-linked recessive trait and shows criss-cross inheritance.
steps: If mother of man is colourblind, then man will also be colourblind as colour blindness is a X-linked recessive trait and shows criss-cross inheritance.
printed_lines: If mother of man is colourblind, then man will also be colourblind as colour blindness is a X-linked
recessive trait and shows criss-cross inheritance.

steps: The colour blind female is homozygous: $X^cX^c$.
The man's mother was colour blind ($X^cX^c$), so she passes $X^c$ to him; the man is $X^cY$ (colour blind).
Cross $X^cX^c \times X^cY$: daughters $X^cX^c$, sons $X^cY$.
All progeny are colour blind, i.e. $100\%$, which is option $2$.

  2. The man's mother was colour blind (XcXc), so she passes Xc to him; the man is XcY (colour blind).
  3. Cross XcXc × XcY: daughters XcXc, sons XcY.
  4. All progeny are colour blind, i.e. 100%, which is option 2.
ai_solution.why: Man's mother was colour blind (XcXc), so he got Xc and is colour blind (XcY); XcXc x XcY gives all children (XcXc daughters, XcY sons) colour blind.

solution.full_text:
1. $1\%$ recombination frequency $=1$ centi Morgan
2. To place the genes on a linear chromosome, decreasing order of recombination frequency will be considered.

1. 1% recombination frequency =1 centi Morgan
  2. To place the genes on a linear chromosome, decreasing order of recombination frequency will be considered.
steps: $1\%$ recombination frequency $=1$ centi Morgan
To place the genes on a linear chromosome, decreasing order of recombination frequency will be considered.
printed_lines: To place the genes on a linear chromosome, decreasing order of recombination frequency will be

steps: Recombination frequency is proportional to map distance, so the farthest pair $a$–$d$ ($29\%$) are the two ends.
$a$–$c = 5\%$ is smallest from $a$, so $c$ lies next to $a$: $a, c, \dots$
$c$–$b = 15\%$ places $b$ after $c$: $a$–$b = 5 + 15 = 20\%$, matching the given value.
$b$–$d = 9\%$ places $d$ last: $c$–$d = 15 + 9 = 24\%$ and $a$–$d = 5 + 15 + 9 = 29\%$, both matching.
The order is $a, c, b, d$, which is option $2$.
ai_solution.html:
1. Recombination frequency is proportional to map distance, so the farthest pair a–d (29%) are the two ends.
  2. a–c = 5% is smallest from a, so c lies next to a: a, c, …
  3. c–b = 15% places b after c: a–b = 5 + 15 = 20%, matching the given value.
  4. b–d = 9% places d last: c–d = 15 + 9 = 24% and a–d = 5 + 15 + 9 = 29%, both matching.
  5. The order is a, c, b, d, which is option 2.
ai_solution.why: Distances are additive along the order a-c-b-d: a-c 5, c-b 15, b-d 9 give a-b 20, c-d 24, a-d 29, all matching.

Check additivity for the whole map: a-c (5) + c-b (15) + b-d (9) = 29 = a-d, and c-d = 15 + 9 = 24, confirming the order a, c, b, d.
